description:
## Problem

`fetch_html` (lines 107–118) rescues `IO::TimeoutError` to return an empty string, but lets `IO::Error` and `Socket::Error` propagate. This is inconsistent because:

1. The caller `process_html_response` has no rescue for these — they'll crash into the outer retry loop's rescue, but the error message will be misleading (treated as a transient fetch failure, not an HTML read failure).

2. Meanwhile, `sanitize_html` (called from `fetch_html`) re-raises `IO::Error | Socket::Error`, which means an IO error during sanitization escapes `fetch_html`'s timeout rescue and hits the retry loop. This is semantically wrong — sanitization errors are not transient network failures and should not be retried.

## Proposed Fix

Make both `fetch_html` and `sanitize_html` handle IO errors consistently:

```crystal
private def fetch_html(body_io : IO) : String
  memory = IO::Memory.new
  IO.copy(body_io, memory, limit: @config.max_size)
  html = memory.to_slice.to_s
  @config.debug("HTML fetched: #{html.size} bytes")
  html = sanitize_html(html)
  @config.debug("HTML sanitized: #{html.size} bytes")
  html
rescue ex : IO::TimeoutError | IO::Error | Socket::Error
  @config.debug("HTML fetch/IO error: #{ex.class} - #{ex.message}")
  ""
end

private def sanitize_html(html : String) : String
  Sanitize::Policy::HTMLSanitizer.common.process(html)
rescue ex : HTML5::HTMLException | URI::Error | IO::Error | Socket::Error
  @config.debug("HTML sanitization failed: #{ex.message}")
  ""
end
```

This ensures IO errors are always treated as empty results (not retried), and keeps the retry loop focused on actual network failures.

## Files
- src/vug/html_extractor.cr (fix fetch_html and sanitize_html)
- spec/vug/extractor_initialization_spec.cr (verify behavior)
title: Fix inconsistent error handling in HtmlExtractor#fetch_html
